claims.text: The initial material is Ti-6Al-4V in a standard annealed condition.
Plasma nitriding at approximately 500°C for 4 hours in a controlled nitrogen/hydrogen atmosphere can produce the proposed surface modification.
Precise control of temperature, gas composition, and treatment time will limit the nitride-layer thickness.
The treatment will form a thin, uniform TiN-enriched surface layer.
The treatment will form a controlled, shallow nitrogen-diffused subsurface zone.
At the proposed nitriding temperature, nitrogen diffuses into Ti-6Al-4V.
Diffusing nitrogen forms a hard TiN phase at the surface and a compositional gradient beneath it.
The TiN-enriched layer and nitrogen diffusion zone increase surface hardness.
The TiN-enriched layer and nitrogen diffusion zone enhance wear resistance.
Tight process control minimizes over-diffusion and the associated risk of deteriorating alloy toughness.
The treatment will increase surface hardness to approximately three to four times that of untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
The treatment will reduce wear rate by at least 50% relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V under high-load dry sliding.
The hardness and wear improvements will be maintained under high-load dry-sliding conditions.
Deviations from the controlled process parameters may cause compromised toughness or insufficient surface modification.
